newsitem.title: USA: Stocks get lift from IBM, oil companies.
newsitem.headline: Stocks get lift from IBM, oil companies.

text.p: Stock prices rose Monday on the back of earnings-driven gains in the shares of International Business Machines Corp. and major oil companies.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 15.28 points at 6,109.51, which surpassed Friday's record close of 6,094.23.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances by a small margin on active volume of 238 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 6.12 points to 1,248.60 and the American Stock Exchange index edged up 0.22 at 579.25.

"We have buoyancy from last week's momentum and steady bonds as well as the IBM earnings, which cast a positive light on the third and fourth quarters," said Charlie Crane, director of research at Spears Benzak Salomon & Farrell.
IBM said it earned $1.3 billion in the third quarter vs. a loss of $500 million a year ago when it was paying for its acquisition of Lotus Development Corp.

The market got an extra boost from comments by IBM's Chief Financial Officer Richard Thoman that he was still "very comfortable" about the firm's prospects for 1996 and its position going forward. IBM was up 3-1/2 at 132-7/8.
"The CFO's comments were encouraging and taken as a bellwether for the industry," Crane said.
Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp., said the fact that market movers such as IBM, Texaco Inc. and Exxon Corp. all posted good earnings was giving the market a push higher.

"A stable bond market, improving earnings -- that's the story of this market," he said, adding that of the 236 companies that reported earnings through last Friday, 121 were higher than expected while 76, or 32 percent, came in below forecasts.

Texaco reported a 50 percent jump in profits to $434 million, and its stock rose 2-1/2 to 106-1/8. Exxon's net income was at a new high for a third quarter of $1.56 billion, topped the previous third quarter record of $1.50 billion a year ago.
Analysts said the high price of oil translated into strong earnings, and the likelihood of a cold winter and more Mideast tension made the group's prospects even better.

"There is a migration into the oil sector. It is drawing media attention to the fact that oil prices have stayed high for a long time despite the fact that many economists were expecting a retreat," Johnson said.
Crude oil was off 4 cents at $25.75 a barrel after jumping initially to $25.95 on the New York Mercantile Exchange.
In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose 5/32 of a point, lowering its yield to 6.79 percent from 6.80 percent on Friday.
The IBM earnings bolstered other high technology stocks. Among them, Sun Microsystems Inc., the most active Nasdaq issue, was up 1-3/8 at 61-3/8.
